data.title: Gremi Media Restructures Credit Line with ING Bank Śląski
data.description:
An update from Gremi Media SA ( (PL:GME) ) is now available.

Gremi Media S.A. has amended its long-standing multiproduct agreement with ING Bank Śląski, reducing the overall credit limit to PLN 1.1 million and narrowing the scope of the facility to bank guarantees only. The term of these guarantees has been extended to late July 2028, with collateral simplified to a single blank promissory note and related declaration, signaling a more streamlined and potentially lower-risk financing structure for the company and its banking partner.

The adjustment of the credit limit and focus on guarantees suggests Gremi Media is aligning its banking facilities more tightly with current operational needs and risk management policies. For stakeholders, the move indicates a controlled and structured approach to leverage, potentially improving transparency and predictability of the company’s financial obligations while maintaining access to essential guarantee instruments for its business activities.

data.title: Steel Dynamics Raises Q3 Earnings Guidance on Strong Demand
data.description:
Steel Dynamics ( (STLD) ) just unveiled an announcement.

On September 17, 2026, Steel Dynamics issued earnings guidance for the third quarter of 2026, forecasting diluted earnings per share of $5.34 to $5.38, up sharply from $3.69 in the second quarter and $2.74 a year earlier, reflecting strong pricing and record steel shipments. The company cited significantly higher profitability in its steel operations driven by wider metal margins and lower scrap costs, resilient demand across non‑residential construction, energy, automotive and industrial sectors, and continued share repurchases totaling $261 million, while planning to release full third‑quarter results on October 19, 2026.

Third‑quarter earnings from metals recycling are expected to decline on lower spreads and shipments, but steel fabrication profits should improve modestly on stronger volumes and a backlog nearly 50 percent above the prior‑year quarter, extending into early 2027. Aluminum earnings are projected to rise on increased shipments as the company ramps its new Columbus, Mississippi flat rolled products mill, with all cold mills and the first CASH line now operating and commercial aluminum shipments slated to begin in the fourth quarter, reinforcing Steel Dynamics’ diversification into aluminum and its positioning for demand tied to infrastructure, onshoring, and domestic manufacturing investment.
